newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Q4 aluminium premium seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Q4 aluminium premium seen falling.

text.p: Taiwan's fourth-quarter aluminium premiums were expected to fall by US$10 per tonne from the third quarter due to rising world prices and slow local demand, Taipei metals traders said on Tuesday.
"Buyers are asking for a US$10 cut on the fourth quarter aluminium premium," a major Taipei-based metal dealer said.
The dealer said buyers were demanding lower aluminium import premiums to cope with a recent rally on the London Metal Exchange.
Taiwan's third-quarter aluminium premiums have ranged about $90-95 per tonne over LME futures prices.
Traders said suppliers and buyers would settle Taiwan's fourth-quarter aluminum import premiums by early September.
"Buyers are asking us to share their cost increases," an aluminium supplier said.
LME three-months aluminium touched a 22-month high at $1,747 per tonne on Monday before ending at $1,744.
Traders said suppliers were likely to agree to buyers' request to cut the premium level as Taiwan's spot commercial aluminium demand has fallen since LME rally.
"Suppliers will have to cut premiums to keep business interest," a trader said.
Taiwan metal traders generally expect the aluminium rally to continue but say a slowdown in China's imports could pressure regional premiums or even the world market.
Traders cited unconfirmed reports that China had canceled or delayed purchase of 50,000 tonnes of Russian aluminium ingots.

"There are some reports saying that a shipment of 50,000 tonnes of Russian aluminium was stalled on its way to China," a buyer said. ***Latest indications of spot import premiums at Taiwan's Keelung or Kaohsiung ports on CIF basis, in US$ per tonne over LME cash prices, are as follows:
